article.articleHeadline: Namibia halts meat exports after rare foot-and-mouth disease outbreak
article.articleSummary: Namibia records its first outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) in its primary commercial livestock zone in six decades, prompting a nationwide ban on livestock movement and meat exports. FMD is a highly contagious viral infection affecting cattle and other cloven-hoofed animals, not dangerous to humans. Namibia becomes the eighth southern African country to be hit by FMD this year, after Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Mozambique, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe. The virus breached Namibia's veterinary cordon fence, crossing from the endemic northern region into the south, an area that had remained officially FMD-free since 1964. Authorities have intensified surveillance, restricted animal movements, and halted meat exports to safeguard regional markets and prevent further spread.

triage.notes: 口蹄疫（FMD）はヒトに感染しない家畜疾患だが、南部アフリカ8か国（ボツワナ、エスワティニ、レソト、モザンビーク、ナミビア、南アフリカ、ザンビア、ジンバブエ）で今年発生が確認されており、地域経済・貿易への影響が大きい。記事の主題はナミビアでの発生（対象国リスト外）だが、ザンビアも今年の発生国として明記されているため verified_locations に含めた。公衆衛生への直接的影響は低いが、家畜貿易制限を伴う広域的なアウトブレイクとして注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Congo-Kinshasa: Vacciner les soignants contre Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo: Vaccinate health workers against Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo has now reached seven provinces, including Sud-Ubangi. In Kisangani, Tshopo province, doctor Victor Kingombe died from Ebola, underscoring the risks faced by frontline health workers, with 12 health professionals previously infected in Tshopo. The government has bolstered the response with 50 million dollars, including 3 million for research, while vaccination of healthcare workers takes center stage. A vaccination campaign began on 19 September, prioritizing frontline staff and evaluating the use of Ervebo vaccine against Bundibugyo virus implicated in the current outbreak. The outbreak has caused about 3,800 deaths. Prime Minister Judith Suminwa announced the funding in New York during the UN General Assembly, as international partners pledged additional support. Public health officials warn about contamination risks from blood and body fluids, PPE use, fatigue, stigma, and community hostility, highlighting vaccination as essential to protect health workers.

article.articleSummary: 62-year-old retired soldier Tejveer Singh of Pannapuri, Hapur, died while receiving treatment at a private hospital in Ghaziabad after four to five days of fever; his family suspects swine influenza. He was first treated in Meerut before being shifted to Ghaziabad; death occurred Thursday night. Health authorities have not confirmed swine flu in his case; the district CMO says there is no record of swine flu treatment or testing in the health portal or from the treating hospital yet. A health team will visit his home on Saturday to gather details and review medical records to determine the cause of death. The district has rising swine flu activity with two deaths reported so far and daily new suspected or confirmed cases. Public health advisories urge avoiding crowds, maintaining hygiene, and seeking medical advice if symptoms appear; final conclusion awaits investigation.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Agnimitra Paul: Stern message to Howrah to prevent dengue! Warning of heavy penalties as soon as water collects in vacant plots and mosquito larvae are found.
article.articleSummary: Dengue re-emerged in Howrah Municipal Corporation area, triggering intensified control measures. West Bengal's Urban Development Deputy Minister Agnimitra Paul urged residents to adopt strict prevention, vowing zero-tolerance for lapses. If rainwater collects in vacant plots and mosquito larvae are found, landowners will face heavy penalties added to their property taxes. The minister also directed residents to routinely clean rooftops, flower pots, discarded refrigerators, and AC trays, and ensure water does not accumulate in garages or under construction sites. In an accompanying waste-management plan, residential dustbins will be removed in favor of keeping bins only at markets; residents must segregate compostable and non-compostable waste and hand it to sanitation workers. The message emphasizes collective responsibility to eradicate dengue in Howrah. Published 2026-09-26.

article.articleHeadline: Enteric infections and childhood stunting: a systematic review and meta-analysis across four pathogen domains
article.articleSummary: Systematic review and meta-analysis across four pathogen domains links enteric infections with early childhood linear growth faltering and stunting in low- and middle-income countries. It draws on cohorts including Malawi (association between asymptomatic infections and growth impairment), rural Bangladesh (diarrheal illness and enteropathogen exposure), the Philippines (environmental enteric dysfunction and stunting), and Ethiopia (soil-transmitted helminths and intestinal protozoa). The analysis highlights pathogens such as Cryptosporidium and enteroaggregative Escherichia coli, as well as broader enteropathogen burdens detected by multiplex real-time PCR. Environmental enteric dysfunction and repeated enteric infections are implicated in impaired growth trajectories, underscoring the need for integrated nutrition, water, sanitation, and hygiene interventions and improved diagnostics in LMICs. Published 2026-09-26.

triage.headline_ja: 腸管感染症と小児の発育阻害:4つの病原体領域にわたる系統的レビューとメタアナリシス

article.articleHeadline: Folha da Região: Estado de São Paulo chega a 37 casos de sarampo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Folha da Região: State of São Paulo reaches 37 measles cases.
article.articleSummary: Measles cases in the State of São Paulo reached 37 in 2026, according to the State Health Secretariat. The latest case is a 42-year-old man, unvaccinated, resident of the state capital, São Paulo. In 2025, the state tallied two measles cases. Measles is a highly contagious viral disease transmitted by airborne droplets, especially in indoor, crowded settings. Typical symptoms include high fever, cough, runny nose (coryza), conjunctivitis, and a red rash that usually appears 7–14 days after exposure. The report highlights vaccination status for the latest case, underscoring ongoing vulnerability despite prior year activity. No death toll is reported. The information reflects ongoing surveillance data for São Paulo state; no details about laboratory confirmation or infection source are provided in the brief.

triage.triage_reason: サンパウロ州で麻疹症例が前年の2件から37件に急増しており、未接種者の感染も確認されているため、流行の可能性と公衆衛生上の懸念からフルリスク評価が必要と判断した。
triage.notes: 州保健局が症例数の増加を公表しており、未接種者の感染例が続く点から今後の拡大リスクに注意が必要。死亡例や検査確定情報は報告されていない。

article.articleHeadline: 禽流感風險高 養禽場防疫啟動 | 中華日報|中華新聞雲
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: High risk of avian influenza; biosecurity measures activated at poultry farms.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-09-26, Tainan City’s Animal Protection and Health Office activated the Autumn-Winter Avian Influenza Enhanced Biosecurity measures, coordinated with the central government, running from September through March 31, 2027. With autumn-winter conditions and migrating wild birds, authorities aim to block viral transmission through pre-emptive preparedness and response phases. Measures include increased sampling of migratory bird droppings, poultry farms, and surrounding environments; reinforced cleaning and disinfection of high-risk areas and farm biosecurity, especially anti-bird facilities; and intensified cleaning/disinfection checks of egg cartons. High-risk districts in Tainan—Xiaying, Liujia, Beimen, Xigang, Jiali, Guantian, Houbi, Madou, Xuejia, Yanshui and nearby wetlands—will see expanded surveillance across land poultry farms, duck farms, and goose farms. The Agriculture Bureau notes autumn-winter is the peak poultry influenza season; to date, over 890 poultry farms inspected and more than 8,200 disinfection events conducted citywide, including disinfecting roads around farms, cargo yards, and wetlands.

article.articleHeadline: تحذير جديد من الصحة العالمية.. ما طبيعة الجائحة المقبلة؟ - اليوم السابع
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A new warning from the World Health Organization: What will be the nature of the next pandemic?
article.articleSummary: The World Health Organization warns the next pandemic is a matter of time, with influenza most likely due to continual mutation and annual emergence of new strains, having historically caused hundreds of deaths. Ebola remains a cross-border concern, with outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported and the risk of spread to other countries. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urges sustained investment in health security amid a global shift of funds toward defense, noting that total military spending reached about $2.7 trillion in 2025 while health preparedness remains underfunded. Despite progress since COVID-19—such as the Pandemic Fund with the World Bank, enhanced surveillance, WHO’s Epidemic Intelligence Center, and BioHub for faster sample sharing—gaps persist. The May 2025 pandemic accord and ongoing PABS negotiations aim to bolster coordination. Reduced official development assistance threatens Ebola response in the DRC, and the U.S. withdrawal from WHO is viewed as a global setback; measles outbreaks in the U.S. and elsewhere highlight vaccine inequities.

triage.headline_ja: WHOからの新たな警告：次のパンデミックはどのような性質になるのか？
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はWHO事務局長による将来的なパンデミックリスクに関する政策的・啓発的な論評であり、DRCのエボラや米国の麻疹について新規具体的な症例情報は含まれず、既存状況への言及に留まる。
triage.notes: 記事はWHOの資金不足・パンデミック備え政策に関する一般論であり、DRCのエボラ継続状況や米国の麻疹アウトブレイクは具体的な新規事例としてではなく背景情報として言及されている。米国は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。続報で具体的な症例・地域情報が出た場合はフルRRAへの移行を検討。

article.articleHeadline: Deadly virus outbreak as 'very high risk' expands and death toll nearly 4,000
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by Bundibugyo virus, has expanded to seven provinces with 7,890 confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths as of Sept 23 (CFR 48.1%; 1,966 recovered). Since Sept 1, 1,133 additional confirmed cases and 532 deaths were reported. Declared in May, this is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the DRC and the second-largest globally, affecting 63 health zones. Border zones Bulu (Sud Ubangi) and Dungu (Haut-Uele) have reported cases, signaling cross-border spread toward Central African Republic and South Sudan. No approved vaccine or licensed antiviral exists for Bundibugyo virus; experimental trials are underway. The seven-day moving average showed a resurgence in early September, followed by a decline. National risk is 'very high'; WHO cautions against travel/trade restrictions and urges cross-border coordination, surveillance, and rapid case management to reduce mortality.

article.articleHeadline: National Health Mission officials reviews dengue prevention work in Tiruchi
article.articleSummary: National Health Mission (NHM) director S. Aneesh Sekhar and Tiruchi Corporation Commissioner N. Ponmani reviewed dengue-prevention measures in Tiruchi, Tamil Nadu, on Saturday, 2026-09-26. Spot checks were conducted in Zone No. 4 covering Patthammal Street, Rajarajeshwari Nagar, Marsingpettai, and Wards 52 and 65, with District Health Officer T. Manivannan and senior officials present. Ponmani urged residents to seek dengue treatment at government hospitals, which were stocked with medicines. As part of the prevention drive, hollow objects that can collect water—discarded vehicle tyres, empty boxes, and other potential water-holding spaces—were disposed of safely. Dengue virus transmission via infected mosquitoes prompted ongoing mosquito-control efforts, including regular fumigation of public spaces in Tiruchi.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mosquito eradication drive to prevent dengue in Kushtia.
article.articleSummary: Three-month dengue prevention drive conducted by Kushtia Municipality in Komalapur area, Ward 1, Kushtia City, on Saturday, 26 September 2026, under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s program. The initiative aims to curb dengue through intensified cleaning and mosquito control. Kushtia Municipal Administrator and Additional Deputy Commissioner (Under-Secretary) Md. Mizanur Rahman led the operation and directed officials to strengthen routine sanitation and vector-control activities. Attendees included Executive Engineer Sohail Rana; Assistant Engineer (Public Works) S.M. Ruhul Amin; Sub-Assistant Engineer (Electric) Md. Jamiul Islam; Conservancy Inspector Md. Sajjad Ahmed, and other municipal staff. Activities targeted stagnant waste and mosquito breeding sites across Komalapur, with emphasis on keeping homes and surroundings clean and preventing water accumulation to reduce dengue transmission.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The United Nations warns of a new pandemic: it's only a matter of time... and we call for an international agreement to confront it
article.articleSummary: As of 26 September 2026, UN leaders at the United Nations convened to review lessons from COVID-19 and pressed for an international Pandemic Agreement led by WHO to strengthen global prevention and preparedness. Vice‑Secretary-General Amina Mohammed warned that no country can insulate itself from a future pandemic and urged equity, solidarity, and multi‑partner collaboration. She noted progress since the 2023 UN General Assembly political declaration, but emphasized that efforts are not yet complete. The warning comes as an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo tests global readiness, reminding that dangerous pathogens remain a critical challenge. The UN highlighted three priorities: closing funding gaps to monitor and contain outbreaks; applying a One Health approach that links human, animal, and environmental health; and ensuring equitable access to life‑saving tools. It called for accelerating negotiations on the international agreement addendum to enhance global crisis response.

triage.headline_ja: 国連、新たなパンデミックを警告：それは時間の問題であり、これに対抗するための国際協定を求める
triage.triage_reason: 記事は国連のパンデミック対策に関する政策的声明が主題であり、DRCのエボラ流行は文脈として言及されているのみで具体的な症例数や地域等の新情報がないため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 本記事は国連の政策提言・国際協定に関する声明が中心であり、DRCのエボラ流行自体の具体的な疫学情報（症例数、地域、致死率等）は記載されていない。既存の流行状況の続報として別途モニタリングが必要。

article.articleHeadline: Rajkot civic body uses drones, AI to identify 4,731 potential mosquito breeding sites - Bilkul Online
article.articleSummary: Rajkot Municipal Corporation (RMC) used drones and AI to identify 4,731 potential mosquito breeding sites across 59.39 sq km in Rajkot to curb dengue, malaria and chikungunya. Of these sites, 1,340 have been covered by field staff for insecticide spraying and source-reduction, while drone spraying has totaled 40 hours 9 minutes. Surveys focus on high-risk wards 11, 18, 3, 4 and 13 within the city’s 161.85 sq km area. Drones inspect drains, waterlogged areas, pits and riverbed depressions - habitats where conventional spraying is challenging. Data are forwarded to ward health workers to verify sites and carry out actions. Conventional vector-control continued Sept 17-23. Field teams, Urban ASHAs and MPHWs larvicided 150,172 houses; fogging occurred at 933 houses; vehicle fogging covered dense areas and sensitive zones. Non-residential premises (409) were inspected, with notices issued to 312 residential and 92 commercial sites and administrative charges recovered.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tshopo: Awareness-raising among households against Ebola in the Kabondo Health Zone - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease is the focus as community relay teams of the Red Cross, Tshopo branch, intensify door-to-door awareness in Kabondo health zone, Kisangani, Democratic Republic of Congo. Since almost a week, teams of three are alerting residents to the danger of Ebola, promoting preventive measures, and outlining the disease's signs and where to seek care for suspected cases. Messages are delivered in Lingala and Swahili during house visits, addressing distrust among some residents who doubt the disease's existence. Zawadi and Wandugu health areas are among the first targeted. The awareness drive comes amid rising confirmed Ebola infections, with the provincial health division reporting 43 confirmed cases, 17 deaths, and 13 recoveries as of Sept 23, 2026.

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية تحذر: الجائحة المقبلة "مسألة وقت".. من أين سيأتي الخطر القادم؟
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization warns: The next pandemic is only a matter of time... Where will the next threat come from?
article.articleSummary: As of 26 September 2026, the World Health Organization warns that the next pandemic is a matter of time and calls for sustained investment in preparedness and early warning, not reactionary response. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus notes no single disease is named, but influenza remains a key concern due to ongoing mutations, while other emerging pathogens are possible. The article highlights ongoing local Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo; a local flare-up does not automatically become a global pandemic, depending on transmissibility and containment. Since COVID-19, WHO and partners have improved readiness: an epidemic fund with the World Bank, enhanced surveillance systems, a BioHub to speed sharing of samples. The May 2025 Pandemic Accord aims to strengthen international coordination, while access to vaccines and diagnostics remains uneven; efforts include transferring mRNA vaccine technology and building local manufacturing capacity.

triage.notes: 記事はWHO事務局長の一般的な将来のパンデミックへの備えに関する発言をまとめたもので、DRCのエボラ流行は既存の事例として言及されているに過ぎず、新規の具体的発生情報ではないため、地域検証の対象外とした。

article.articleHeadline: Influenza A Masuk Bandung, 65 Kasus Positif Terdeteksi, Gejalanya Lebih Berat dari Flu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza A Enters Bandung, 65 Positive Cases Detected, Its Symptoms Are More Severe Than the Flu.
article.articleSummary: As of 26 September 2026, Influenza A has entered Bandung, West Java, with at least 65 laboratory-confirmed cases in Kota Bandung. The figures are confirmed by Raden Vini Adiani Dewi, head of the West Java Health Office. Authorities urge calm but vigilance, noting that Influenza A differs from ordinary flu and can cause more severe symptoms, including headache, high fever, body aches, and fatigue; the circulating strain is associated with H1N1-like influenza A. Bandung’s Dinas Kesehatan is implementing targeted responses; surveillance centers on Puskesmas Padasuka, where influenza patients are swabbed and samples sent to Jakarta’s Ministry of Health to confirm the strain. Pending results, data will include Influenza A, Influenza B, and COVID-19, though COVID-19 is not detected. Officials say Influenza A is endemic in Bandung, but cases at one clinic may not reflect citywide trends; similar activity has been observed in Surabaya and Makassar.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザAがバンドンに流入、65例の陽性が検出、症状は通常のインフルエンザより重い

article.articleHeadline: Mesmo com pior epidemia da década, só 16,3% das doses contra chikungunya foram aplicadas em MS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Even with the worst epidemic of the decade, only 16.3% of doses against chikungunya were administered in Mato Grosso do Sul.
article.articleSummary: Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, recorded 31 chikungunya deaths and 10,367 confirmed cases in 2026, the worst outbreak of the decade. Vaccination remains limited: 64,452 doses were received, but only 10,494 were administered (16.3%) across six municipalities—Sete Quedas, Amambai, Douradina, Itaporã, Dourados, and Batayporã; Dourados led with 5,715 doses. The state also reported 119 pregnant women among cases, with one death under investigation. Total probable cases in 2026 reached 12,120, about 86% of 2025’s 14,100. El Niño conditions could fuel a new surge, as higher temperatures likely boost Aedes aegypti transmission, potentially extending into 2027. Chikungunya (CHIKV) is transmitted by infected female Aedes aegypti; symptoms include high fever and severe joint pain, with possible cardiovascular, renal, dermatological, and neurological complications. Diagnostic tests exist; vaccination stock remains in state and municipal networks.

triage.headline_ja: 10年で最悪の流行にもかかわらず、マット・グロッソ・ド・スル州ではチクングニア熱ワクチンの接種率は16.3%にとどまる

triage.notes: 記事はブラジル・マット・グロッソ・ド・スル州における2026年チクングニア熱流行（死者31名、確定症例10,367件）とワクチン接種率の低さ（16.3%）を報じている。エルニーニョによる媒介蚊増加で2027年への流行拡大が懸念される。国際的拡大や渡航制限の言及はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Sudah Ada Kasus Super Flu Ditemukan di Semarang, Batita
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: There have already been cases of Super Flu found in Semarang, Batita.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A (H3N2) subclade K, nicknamed 'super flu', was detected in Semarang, Central Java, Indonesia. A child under three years old (2 years 9 months) treated at RSUP Dr Kariadi Semarang in December 2025 tested serologically positive, with laboratory confirmation in March 2026. As of September 26, 2026, no additional cases have been reported in Central Java. The patient exhibited severe flu symptoms with comorbidities. Health official Zulfachmi Wahab says the finding prompts increased surveillance but cautions against alarm, noting no ongoing outbreak like COVID-19. Detections have also occurred in East Java, West Java, and Jakarta, largely linked to expanded screening. Authorities urge continued monitoring and screening at hospitals and primary care facilities, especially during the dry season.

article.articleHeadline: ما هو الوباء القادم؟.. الصحة العالمية تحذر: الجائحة المقبلة مسألة وقت - الأسبوع
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What is the next epidemic? WHO warns: the upcoming pandemic is only a matter of time - The Week
article.articleSummary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that the next pandemic is a matter of when, not if, urging sustained investments in health security as global defense spending rises. He noted 2025 military expenditure around $2.7 trillion and warned that underinvestment in health readiness hampers outbreak responses. Some progress since COVID-19 includes the May 2025 Pandemic Accord negotiations, the WHO hub for outbreak intelligence, the BioHub for rapid sample sharing, and a vaccine-technology transfer initiative that will bolster local production in South Korea to improve equity. He cited the ongoing PABS negotiations and stressed that tools for diagnostics and vaccines should not be treated as charity. He criticized the U.S. withdrawal from WHO and warned that measles outbreaks in the United States and elsewhere reflect preventable deaths. A >40% decline in official development assistance has weakened Ebola responses in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

article.articleHeadline: Jangan Selalu Anggap Masuk Angin, Batuk Bisa Jadi Gejala Pneumonia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Don't Always Assume It's Just a Cold; Coughing Could Be a Symptom of Pneumonia.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia faces pneumonia awareness gaps as coughing is often treated as a common cold. In Jakarta, health experts warn that pneumococcal pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae can rapidly damage lung tissue and fill alveoli with fluid, triggering acute shortness of breath and, in severe cases, chest pain and confusion. A YouGov survey cited in the article found 41% of Indonesian adults have never heard of pneumonia. The misconception of ‘paru-paru basah’ as night-time exposure rather than fluid buildup leads to delays in care. Diagnosis requires clinical evaluation and laboratory tests; early outpatient care is insufficient in high-risk groups. People over 60, and those with diabetes, asthma, cardiovascular disease, or stroke history, should seek urgent evaluation if symptoms persist beyond 3–4 days, or if there is severe dyspnea or sudden confusion.

article.articleHeadline: Flu in children: What parents needs to know - The Tribune
article.articleSummary: Influenza in India this season is predominantly linked to H1N1; testing gaps mean actual burden may be higher. India’s flu season typically peaks January–March and August–October, with current rise following the usual pattern. A 2009–2017 Christian Medical College, Vellore analysis found children under 5 years old accounted for 64.8% of cases, 82.5% of hospital admissions, and 79.3% of deaths from influenza. Typical pediatric symptoms include sudden high fever (often 100–104°F), chills, dry cough, sore throat, body aches, fatigue, and vomiting or diarrhea; infants may have fever as the main sign. Emergency cues are fast or labored breathing, bluish lips, severe muscle pain, dehydration, altered consciousness, seizures, or fever >104°F not responding to treatment. Rebound improvement followed by worse suggests secondary infections like bacterial pneumonia. Prevention emphasizes annual vaccine (with H1N1 component), hand hygiene, masking, early antiviral treatment within 48 hours, staying home when sick, and avoiding aspirin in children.

article.articleHeadline: सतना अस्पताल की मेजर ओटी में मिले फंगस और बैक्टीरिया, ऑपरेशन बंद, जानें कब शुरू होगा
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fungus and bacteria detected in the major operating theatre of Satna Hospital; surgery halted; know when it will resume.
article.articleSummary: As of 26 September 2026, Satna District Hospital’s Major Operating Theatre has suspended surgeries after fungus and bacteria were detected. Microbiology culture from eight sites—including floors, walls, the OT table, OT lights, and equipment—returned positive for bacteria, with fungus linked to seepage and water leakage in the old building. Water-proofing and repainting have been underway for about 10 days, with rain delaying a second coat. Following the culture results, intensive cleaning, disinfection, and fumigation are in progress; after fumigation, re-sampling will determine if infections are cleared, with reopening of the OT expected on Monday if conditions are normal. The Modular OT’s laminar flow has been nonfunctional for 8–10 days, prompting specialist engineers to intervene. Emergency cases and maternity deliveries (cesarean) continue in the maternity OT and the operating suite, while several elective surgeries face delays.}

article.articleHeadline: Le Vietnam déploie un vaccin pour protéger les jeunes enfants contre la maladie pieds-mains-bouche
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Vietnam rolls out a vaccine to protect young children against hand-foot-and-mouth disease.
article.articleSummary: Vietnam launched Envacgen, a vaccine against hand-foot-and-mouth disease primarily caused by enterovirus 71 (EV71), on Sept 25, 2026, across nearly 300 VNVC vaccination centers nationwide. Approved by the Ministry of Health for children aged two months to under six years, the regimen is two or three doses by age. Phase 3 trials in Vietnam showed 96.8% efficacy against EV71-associated HFMD, with no EV71 infections among vaccinated participants and strong immune responses to multiple EV71 subgenotypes. The study enrolled over 3,000 children, mainly Vietnamese, with a favorable safety profile and durable protection in follow-up. Taiwan has used the EV71 vaccine with over 600,000 doses (Aug 2023–Sept 2026) and ongoing post-vaccination surveillance confirming safety and effectiveness. In Vietnam, HFMD remains a major illness in young children; 2023 data reported >181,000 cases and 31 deaths, with EV71 accounting for most hospitalizations and severe cases.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Under the directives of the Head of State, the UAE allocates $10 million to support international efforts to curb the Ebola epidemic.
article.articleSummary: Under the directives of UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the United Arab Emirates allocated US$10 million through the UAE International Aid Agency to bolster international efforts to curb the Ebola epidemic in Africa and strengthen health-response capacities in affected areas. The announcement came during an international meeting convened at the invitation of the United States to discuss Ebola developments and bolster global response, in the United Nations General Assembly context. The UAE has shipped more than 150 metric tons of aid and diverse supplies—protective equipment, infection-control materials, and containment tools—benefiting about 280 health facilities, along with shelter and food provisions for affected populations, including women and children. Health authorities in the DRC say they are continuing their efforts to combat the outbreak, maintaining a response to the disease as the situation persists.

article.articleHeadline: HKU5-CoV-2: Mysteriöses Fledermaus-Virus entdeckt - Wissenschaftler warnen vor Übersprung
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: HKU5-CoV-2: Mysterious Bat Virus Discovered — Scientists Warn of Spillover
article.articleSummary: HKU5-CoV-2, a newly identified bat coronavirus found in Brazilian bats, carries a functional furin cleavage site on its Spike protein, a feature associated with SARS-CoV-2. There are no documented human infections or any evidence of human-to-human transmission to date. In laboratory tests, HKU5-CoV-2 can enter human lung and intestinal cells via mechanisms similar to SARS-CoV-2, but its efficiency is notably lower. The virus shows the ability to bind to receptors across multiple mammal species, raising concerns about zoonotic spillover if it mutates. Researchers note the natural occurrence of furin sites in bat coronaviruses, arguing against claims that COVID-19 originated in a laboratory. Although the immediate risk to the population remains low, experts emphasize vigilance given drivers of spillover, and say vaccines could be developed rapidly if human transmission begins.

triage.headline_ja: HKU5-CoV-2:謎のコウモリウイルスを発見 ― 科学者らがヒトへの飛び火(スピルオーバー)に警鐘

article.articleHeadline: UAE allocates $10 million to support international efforts to contain Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-09-26, the UAE allocated $10 million via the UAE Aid Agency to support international efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak in Africa and strengthen affected health systems, with focus on the Democratic Republic of the Congo where the outbreak’s geographic spread is widening. The funding was announced during the UAE’s participation in an international meeting convened by the United States on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly to discuss the Ebola response. Dr Tareq Ahmed Al Ameri, Chairman of the UAE Aid Agency, said the UAE is actively supporting joint international actions to address crises and health challenges globally. To date, the UAE has sent more than 150 tonnes of aid and supplies, including protective equipment, infection-control materials, shelter supplies, and food, benefiting around 280 health facilities and affected people. The UAE called for stronger international coordination and faster action to limit transmission and bolster prevention and early detection in the outbreak area.

article.articleHeadline: 18 Kasus Influenza Tipe A Ditemukan di DIY, Warga Diminta Waspadai Flu Musiman Ini
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 18 Cases of Influenza A Detected in DIY, Residents Urged to Be Wary of This Seasonal Influenza.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A has been detected in 18 people in the DI Yogyakarta (DIY) region as of 23 September 2026, part of the year-round seasonal influenza circulating in Indonesia. Cases were identified through sentinel site surveillance for influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) at designated health facilities, under the national program. Symptoms align with seasonal flu, including fever, cough, and sore throat. There has been no week-to-week increase over the last four weeks. Health authorities advise calm and ongoing preventive measures: practice PHBS (handwashing with soap and running water), cough etiquette (mask use and covering the mouth when coughing or sneezing), and general immune-boosting actions. The DI Yogyakarta Dinas Kesehatan is coordinating with networks to bolster public education via media. No specifics on transmission sources or imported/exported cases are provided.

triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザのサーベイランス報告であり、通常の年間循環の範囲内。週次増加なしと明記されており、公衆衛生上の緊急性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Les USA débloquent 267 millions $ supplémentaires contre Ebola en Afrique centrale
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The United States allocates an additional $267 million to fight Ebola in Central Africa.
article.articleSummary: The United States commits an additional 267 million USD to Ebola response in Central Africa, primarily for the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), bringing U.S. support to 886 million USD and aligning with a broader 2-billion-dollar regional goal. The outbreak, detected in May, is the second-deadliest Ebola wave, after West Africa 2014–2016. As of September 23 per WHO, the DRC has 7,890 confirmed cases and 3,779 deaths; Ituri remains the hardest hit, while Nord-Kivu has surged, reporting 567 cases in the 21 days to September 23. Transmission may involve the rare Bundibugyo virus; authorities suspect circulation for months before first confirmed Ituri cases. The epidemic has spread to Sud-Ubangi; response remains hampered by security constraints, surveillance gaps, lack of vaccines/treatments, and armed conflict. Efforts include treatment centers, diagnostics, health-worker supplies, contact tracing, and risk communication; Uganda declared end of its outbreak on July 28, but reintroduction risk persists.

article.articleHeadline: "养砖头" 很治愈？医生：切莫忽视真菌带来的健康风险
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "Raising bricks" is very therapeutic? Doctor: Do not ignore the health risks posed by fungi.
article.articleSummary: “Raising bricks” in Jiangsu, China, a low-cost stress-relief trend involving damp bricks with moss, raises health concerns as users report sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes. Jiangsu Provincial People’s Hospital ENT physician Wang Yunli explains moist moss on bricks creates an ideal host for fungi such as Aspergillus; inhaled spores can trigger allergic rhinitis and allergic conjunctivitis, with symptoms including paroxysmal sneezing, watery rhinorrhea, nasal itching, obstruction, and eye itching/redness. In immunocompromised individuals, fungi may colonize and invade, causing invasive fungal infections of the respiratory tract, lungs, or brain. Fungal sinusitis may present with foul odor and dark secretions seen after surgical access to sinuses. Skin contact can cause dermatitis or infection if skin is breached; brick surfaces may carry tetanus bacillus, Legionella, or Staphylococcus. Precautions include ventilated placement, masks during handling, hand washing, and saline nasal irrigation; those with allergies, asthma, or immune suppression should avoid. Humid areas near Nanjing have higher fungal prevalence.

article.articleHeadline: कूलर, गमले, पुराने टायरों में छिपा डेंगू का खतरा, कठुआ में नया केस; 44 हुए डेंगू-मलेरिया के मामले, घर-घर जांच शुरू - kathua dengue cases rise to 44 health dept intensifies efforts
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue danger hidden in coolers, flower pots, and old tires; a new case in Kathua; dengue and malaria cases rise to 44; door-to-door checks begin - Kathua dengue cases rise to 44; Health Department intensifies efforts.
article.articleSummary: As of 26 September 2026, Kathua district reports a dengue surge with 26 dengue cases and a total of 44 dengue-malaria cases. The latest dengue case is from Shiv Nagar Ward No. 16 in Kathua town; 40-year-old Suresh Kumar, a resident of Bani now living in Shiv Nagar, tested positive and is being treated at GMC Kathua. In response, the Health Department conducts anti-larvae spraying around the patient’s home and nearby areas, and accelerates awareness campaigns. District officials, including Chief Medical Officer Dr. Vijay Raina and District Health Officer Dr. Uttam Chand, supervise field teams under DMO Sohan Lal; Flying Squad teams conduct door-to-door surveys to identify larval sites. The teams inspect potential larval habitats like coolers, flower pots, old tires, water drums, etc., and apply anti-larvicide where needed. Residents urged to remove standing water and seek prompt testing for fever, dengue, or malaria symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: الأمم المتحدة تدعو إلى سد فجوات تمويل التأهب للجوائح وتعزيز التعاون الدولي لمواجهة الأوبئة المستقبلية - بوابة الأهرام
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The United Nations Calls for Filling Gaps in Pandemic Preparedness Financing and Strengthening International Cooperation to Face Future Pandemics - Al-Ahram Portal
article.articleSummary: UN calls to fill funding gaps in pandemic preparedness and secure sustainable resources for prevention, surveillance, and response, while boosting international cooperation against future pandemics. In a message from Secretary-General Antonio Guterres delivered by Deputy Amina Mohammed at a New York meeting during the General Assembly, the UN stressed that Covid-19 proved no country can protect itself alone in a connected world. Readiness must be permanent, based on equity, solidarity, and multilateral cooperation. Progress since the 2023 political declaration includes amendments to the International Health Regulations and the WHO Pandemic Accord, with negotiations on a pathogen access and benefit-sharing system ongoing. Yet Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo underscored ongoing gaps. Funding often rises with crises and recedes afterward, weakening preparedness. The call: adopt One Health, accelerate finalizing access-and-benefit sharing, and ensure universal life-saving tools and resources for all countries; preparedness cannot wait for the next crisis.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Mambasa: un laboratoire de diagnostic désormais opérationnel - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Mambasa: a diagnostic laboratory now operational - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease laboratory diagnostics are now available in the Mambasa health zone, Ituri province, northeast Democratic Republic of the Congo, according to local civil society spokesperson Jospin Paluku. The newly operational diagnostic laboratory will yield Ebola results within 24 hours for suspected cases, enabling rapid confirmation or exclusion and directing patient management accordingly. Paluku warned that previously cases were treated without timely confirmation and urged residents of Mambasa and nearby areas to seek care at health facilities at the first signs of illness. A positive result will lead to appropriate Ebola-specific treatment, while delayed care risks further transmission to relatives and the wider community. The Civil Society group urged adherence to preventive practices and early presentation to healthcare facilities to curb spread. ACP report, 26 September 2026.

article.articleHeadline: UAE allocates $10 million to tackle Ebola outbreak as it lifts Uganda travel restrictions | The National
article.articleSummary: UAE pledges $10 million through the UAE Aid Agency to curb the Ebola outbreak in Africa, announced on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly as nations coordinate the international response. The contribution supports the Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where transmission continues, with the UAE having shipped more than 150 tonnes of aid—protective equipment, infection-control materials and food—to affected areas, benefiting about 280 health centres. Dr. Tareq Al Ameri, chairman of UAE Aid Agency, calls for accelerated international support to strengthen prevention, early detection and intervention. Uganda lifts entry restrictions for Ugandan citizens after its Ebola outbreak is declared over; precautionary measures remain for travellers from the DR Congo and South Sudan, with Ncema coordinating risk-based adjustments. The Ebola virus causes severe haemorrhagic fever, and Uganda has experienced several outbreaks in the past two decades.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Bunia : renforcement d'une école en outils de prévention - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Bunia: Strengthening a School in the Use of Prevention Tools
article.articleSummary: As of 26 September 2026, in Bunia, capital of Ituri Province in northeast Democratic Republic of the Congo, an Ebola virus disease (EVD) prevention initiative was strengthened at a local school. The National Institute of Public Health (INSP), through the Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (COUSP), distributed prevention materials—30 image boxes, 20 banners, 1,000 posters, and 20 megaphones—with Caritas support to sustain Ebola messaging for students and staff. The aim is for the school to regularly relay information on Ebola symptoms, transmission, and prevention to families and surrounding communities. During the activity, 1,862 students were sensitized about the disease’s signs, routes of transmission, and protective measures. Messages are designed to be amplified within the school to broader community networks.

article.articleHeadline: RDC/Ebola : le gouvernement approuve le nouveau plan de préparation et de riposte
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC/Ebola: the government approves the new preparedness and response plan.
article.articleSummary: DRC approves a new 180-day multisectoral 'One Health' preparedness and response plan for Ebola virus disease caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, launched in September 2026. The plan provides a common reference framework for ongoing prevention and response activities and includes review of the current epidemiological situation, noting a downward trend in affected provinces except North Kivu, which continues to report cases. The government, via the Ministry of Health, also announces a phased rollout of free healthcare in Ituri for the duration of the Ebola outbreak, initially in Bunia and Rwampara, with expansion contingent on medicine and human-resource availability. By month’s end, partner-supplied medicines are expected to enable free-care in Ituri. Kinshasa is identified as a high-risk zone, prompting reinforced preparedness, and emphasis on engaging religious leaders to bolster community awareness and response.

triage.notes: 発生地域にRwanda（Kigali Province）が含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRC国内（Ituri、North Kivu、Kinshasa）のみが言及されており、Rwandaは主題ではないため除外。既存の継続中アウトブレイクに対する政府の対応計画に関する続報であり、新規発生ではない点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue cases decline, attack rate drops in Coimbatore Corporation
article.articleSummary: Dengue cases in Coimbatore Corporation declined from 124 in the earlier three-week period to 90 in the latest three-week period (-34 cases, -27%). The average weekly attack rate fell from 2.07 to 1.50 per lakh population (-28%). The reduction follows sustained vector-control and surveillance across five zones and 100 wards, with 1,209 dengue-control workers deployed for door-to-door source reduction and 60.65 lakh potential breeding containers removed. Under Operation Shield, fever-affected areas receive intensified vector-control measures, including fogging, medical camps, and awareness activities. A 24-hour fever control centre monitors cases; fogging, source reduction, and awareness continue, with weekly reviews of dengue prevention measures. No lab-confirmed outbreak details or infection sources provided. These actions reflect ongoing dengue management efforts in Coimbatore Corporation.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱症例が減少、コインバトール市の発症率が低下
triage.triage_reason: デング熱症例数・発症率ともに減少傾向にあり、既存の対策が奏功していることを示す内容で、新規性や異常性、深刻な公衆衛生上の懸念は認められない。
triage.notes: 地域の風土病であるデング熱の定例的なサーベイランス報告であり、症例数は減少傾向。緊急対応や国際的な関心を要する内容ではない。

article.articleHeadline: الإمارات تخصص 10 ملايين دولار لمكافحة إيبولا في أفريقيا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The UAE allocates $10 million to combat Ebola in Africa.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak response: United Arab Emirates allocates $10 million via the UAE International Aid Agency to curb Ebola in Africa and strengthen health systems. The pledge, announced during a United States–hosted international meeting at the United Nations General Assembly in New York, targets regions affected by Ebola with emphasis on rapid response and early detection. The move accompanies more than 150 tons of aid shipped to affected areas, benefiting about 280 health facilities and supplying PPE, infection-control materials, shelter, and food for affected people across age groups, including women and children. The outbreak persists in the Democratic Republic of Congo and has been reported in Uganda, with the World Health Organization providing ongoing updates. The UAE calls for intensified international cooperation to accelerate delivery of supplies and coordinate health authorities and international partners to reduce transmission.

triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で継続中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクに対し、国連総会での国際会議を通じてUAEが多額の資金拠出を発表しており、WHOも継続的に状況更新を行う重大な公衆衛生上の懸念事案であるため。

article.articleHeadline: Guarujá antecipa Operação Checkout e amplia combate ao Aedes aegypti
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Guarujá advances Operation Checkout and expands the fight against Aedes aegypti.
article.articleSummary: Guarujá, Brazil; Operation Checkout expanded to inspect 141 hotels and guesthouses before summer to curb Aedes aegypti, with 55 sites inspected so far. Initiated by the Sesau Endemias team and accelerated due to El Niño climate shifts, the preventive measures aim to eliminate breeding sites ahead of higher tourist inflows. Dengue cases in 2026 reached 1,081 (vs 3,060 in the same period of 2025); chikungunya had 2 cases (vs 141 in 2025); Zika remained at 0 in both years. Core strategies include free installation of water-tank screens, cemetery vector control, and biological control by introducing Poecilia reticulata (guppy) fish to large reservoirs and standing water to prey on larvae. These ongoing actions reflect a broader effort to reduce arbovirus transmission through environmental management and natural predation ahead of peak season.

triage.notes: 症例数は前年比で大幅減少しており、通常の季節前予防対策（蚊駆除・環境管理）に関する記事。

article.articleHeadline: Focarul de Ebola din RD Congo se extinde în două noi zone sanitare (OMS)
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is spreading to two new health zones (WHO).
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola caused by Bundibugyo strain in the Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to two new health zones, Bulu (Sud-Ubangi) and Dungu (Haut-Uele), bringing affected zones to 63 across seven provinces, according to WHO. As of 23 September, DRC reported 7,890 laboratory-confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said ongoing regional conflict and population movements hinder access to communities and high-risk contact identification, risking missed transmission chains. While reported infections are declining and contact tracing, safe burials, and community engagement have improved, transmission remains uneven. A lack of vaccines and approved treatments for the Bundibugyo strain complicates response and may fuel care-seeking reluctance; WHO is accelerating vaccine/treatment studies. The pandemic accord adopted May 2025; officials caution against misinformation and urge pandemic preparedness globally.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行、2つの新たな保健地区に拡大（WHO）
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC7州63保健地区に拡大し、死者3,799人・確認症例7,890人と深刻な公衆衛生上の影響があり、紛争による対応困難やワクチン・治療薬不足で国際的拡大リスクも高いため。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株による大規模流行で、7州63保健地区に拡大。ワクチン・治療薬未承認、紛争による接触者追跡困難など長期化リスクが高い。既存の大規模アウトブレイクの継続報道であり、フルリスク評価が必要。

triage.triage_reason: ウクライナの症例は既知病原体（SARS-CoV-2、パラインフルエンザ、アデノ・ライノウイルス、RSV）による季節性ARVIであり対象国にも該当しないため除外。中国で報告された新規マダニ媒介ウイルス(ALTNV)は新規病原体の同定という点で異常性があるが、症例数・重症度・伝播状況の情報が乏しく、続報を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola v Kongu neustává. Úřadům se nedaří dohledat většinu potenciálně nakažených
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo continues unabated. Authorities are unable to trace most of the potentially infected.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continues unabated as tracing of transmission chains remains severely incomplete. Officials estimate more than 400,000 people could be infected or exposed, but investigators have identified only about 30,000 contacts. With around 60 contacts tracked per confirmed case, the current tally of roughly 7,000 infections implies a contact-list shortfall well over 400,000. Africa CDC Director Jean Kaseya warns that, without effective contact tracing, the epidemic cannot be controlled. The virus has spread to new zones, including Bulu in Sud-Ubangi and Dungu in Haut-Uele near the South Sudan border, bringing the outbreak to 63 zones across seven provinces. Some improvement is reported in Ituri, though overall transmission remains serious. International donors pledged nearly $2.9 billion to fight Ebola, including $886 million from the United States.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行が止まらない。当局は感染者の大半を追跡できていない

triage.notes: 記事はDRCにおけるエボラ流行の拡大と接触者追跡の困難、国際支援（29億ドル規模）について報告。South Sudan、United Statesは資金拠出・国境近接の文脈で言及されているのみで発生国ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Ciri-ciri Penyakit Super Flu dan Kapan Harus ke Dokter
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Symptoms of the Super Flu and When to See a Doctor
article.articleSummary: On 26 September 2026, Indonesian health authorities clarify that the term 'Super Flu' does not correspond to a distinct medical disease. It refers to Influenza A infections; however, World Health Organization and the U.S. CDC do not recognize 'Super Flu' as a separate condition. There is no clinical evidence that Influenza A is more dangerous than other influenza strains. Because Influenza A symptoms closely resemble other acute respiratory infections, distinguishing it without testing is challenging. Definitive identification requires laboratory confirmation, such as antigen swab tests or a PCR panel. The article emphasizes seeking medical care when appropriate, and points to a video that discusses symptoms and when to see a doctor. The discussion originates from Indonesia's Ministry of Health statements by Aji Muhawarman, noting the need for lab tests to determine the circulating virus.

triage.triage_reason: 内容はインフルエンザAに関する一般的な健康啓発情報であり、'スーパーフル'という特別な疾患は存在しないことを説明する記事。異常な流行や公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 記事はインドネシア保健省が『スーパーフル』という用語が医学的に独立した疾患ではないことを説明する啓発的内容であり、具体的な感染事例やアウトブレイクの報告は含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: По Украине распространяется неизвестная инфекция: врач рассказал, как она начинается -- симптомы
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: An unknown infection is spreading across Ukraine: a doctor explained how it begins — symptoms.
article.articleSummary: Unknown respiratory illness in Ukraine is rising, with patients not testing positive for COVID-19 or influenza, according to Dr. Zhivaretsky, who shared observations on Facebook. The illness may begin with a mild fever (~37.1°C), nasal congestion, weakness and fatigue, followed by cough after a few days. Early symptoms can resemble allergy; after 3–4 days a bacterial superinfection with higher fever and toxicity may emerge. If symptoms do not improve, testing is advised to guide treatment. In Ukraine (3–30 August 2026), sentinel surveillance recorded 218 influenza-like illness and 201 severe acute respiratory infections; laboratory testing identified SARS-CoV-2, parainfluenza viruses, adenoviruses, rhinoviruses, and RSV. China reports a newly identified tick-borne virus, Asian longhorned tick-associated nairovirus (ALTNV), causing fever and fatigue with gastrointestinal symptoms; 38% of patients had thrombocytopenia, indicating bleeding risk. ALTNV is described as a recently identified pathogen.

article.articleHeadline: Satpol PP Probolinggo Pasang Banner 'Kawasan Bebas Prostitusi', 5 PSK Ternyata Positif HIV
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Probolinggo Satpol PP Puts Up Banner 'Prostitution-Free Zone', 5 Sex Workers Were Found HIV-Positive
article.articleSummary: Probolinggo, East Java, Indonesia: On 2026-09-26, Satpol PP installed a 'Prostitution-Free Zone' banner after arresting 11 sex workers at Emi or Embung Miring in Banjar Sawah, Tegalsiwalan. Health screening, conducted with the Dinas Kesehatan (Dinkes) of Probolinggo, identified five HIV-positive sex workers among those tested. The operation, part of ongoing anti-prostitution mapping, targeted locations where workers wait for clients, with reported rates around 100,000 IDR per encounter. The banner aims to deter reoccupation of the site, and officials say monitoring will continue with potential legal action if the banner is damaged. The report highlights HIV prevalence among sex workers in this locale and the intersection of law enforcement and public health responses in Probolinggo."}{

article.articleHeadline: Ebola death toll in DR Congo rises to 3,833 as cases surpass 7,900
article.articleSummary: Outbreak: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues, with the health ministry reporting 3,833 deaths and 7,946 confirmed cases as of 24 September. The fatality rate among recorded infections stands at 48.2%. DR Congo authorities say they are maintaining surveillance and response efforts to curb transmission in a country already hard-hit by the outbreak since it first appeared there. The figures come from the Ministry of Health’s online update dated September 24, illustrating the ongoing, high-burden toll of Ebola in the region. The report emphasizes that the outbreak remains active and requires sustained public health action, though it does not provide additional details on infection sources or regional case distribution.

article.articleHeadline: RDC : Des hippopotames retrouvés morts dans le Parc national des Virunga
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: Hippos Found Dead in Virunga National Park
article.articleSummary: Several hippopotamuses have been found dead in the Semuliki River within Virunga National Park, Nord-Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. A Sept 24, 2026 statement from the Institut congolais pour la conservation de la nature says the death cause is unknown and urges vigilance from health authorities and local communities. This follows an anthrax episode recorded in April 2025 near Lake Edward. Authorities warn people not to touch carcasses, not to sell meat, and to avoid using water near the remains. A confirmed anthrax case was reported in the Vitshumbi fishing enclave on Aug 14, 2026, after a hippo carcass was found Aug 8, per the Zone de santé de Kibirizi. Experts recommend incinerating cadavers with controlled sites to prevent further contamination and to avoid burying them.

triage.triage_reason: 炭疽菌によるカバの死亡が確認され地域住民への警戒が呼びかけられているが、人への感染拡大や重症度に関する詳細情報が不足しているため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 2025年4月にも同地域で炭疽菌エピソードが発生しており、2026年8月には確定症例も報告されている。カバの原因不明死が継続しており、人への感染拡大リスクについて続報の確認が必要。オーストラリアの地域情報はノイズと判断し除外。

article.articleHeadline: Bệnh dại đã phát bệnh gần như không thể cứu nhưng hoàn toàn có thể phòng ngừa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rabies, once symptoms appear, is almost always fatal, but completely preventable.
article.articleSummary: Rabies remains almost always fatal after symptoms but is fully preventable with timely vaccination and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). On 26 September 2026 in Buôn Ma Thuột, Đắk Lắk Province, Vietnam, the Ministry of Health, with the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development and local authorities, held a national multisector event and drill to strengthen rabies control. Globally, about 59,000 people die annually in more than 150 countries, with roughly 40% under 15 years old. In Vietnam, 2025 recorded 77 deaths; in the first nine months of 2026, 55 deaths occurred. Deaths often follow not receiving or delaying vaccination and improper wound care; access to preventive services remains limited in remote areas. Vietnam aims to eliminate dog- and cat-transmitted human rabies by 2030, requiring simple public messaging, immediate wound care, prompt medical consultation, and expanded PEP access, especially for children and the poor, with cross-sector coordination.

triage.triage_reason: ベトナム保健省による狂犬病予防啓発キャンペーン・訓練イベントの報道であり、新規アウトブレイクや異常事態を示すものではない。狂犬病は既知の風土病で年次統計として報告されている。
triage.notes: 狂犬病はヒト-ヒト感染しない人畜共通感染症であり、記事内容は既存の公衆衛生課題に対する政府主導の啓発・予防強化イベントの報道。2030年までの犬猫媒介狂犬病撲滅目標に向けた取り組みとして位置づけられており、突発的なアウトブレイクのシグナルではない。

article.articleHeadline: UAE Eases Entry Measures for Uganda Nationals After Ebola Outbreak Ends, Says NCEMA MoHAP ICP
article.articleSummary: UAE eases precautionary entry measures for Ugandan nationals after Uganda’s Ebola outbreak ends, while keeping restrictions for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan. The move, announced by NCEMA in coordination with MoHAP and ICP, follows the end of the Ebola outbreak in Uganda after the internationally established monitoring period. Precautionary measures for DR Congo and South Sudan remain in effect due to ongoing epidemiological risk. UAE will continue to monitor regional and international Ebola developments, with measures kept under review and adjustable per evolving risk assessments and public health standards. The changes reflect a proportionate response to current risk while safeguarding public health. Affected locations: UAE, Uganda, DR Congo, South Sudan.

triage.triage_reason: 記事の主題はUAEの渡航規制緩和という行政措置であり、ウガンダの流行は終息済み。DRCと南スーダンには依然として予防的措置が継続中とされるが、具体的な症例数や新規発生の詳細情報がなく、判断材料が不足している。
triage.notes: 記事はUAEの入国規制緩和に関する行政的発表が中心。ウガンダの流行は終息と明記されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCは『ongoing epidemiological risk』として言及されているものの、具体的な症例情報は本文に含まれず、継続的な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: الإمارات تعلن تخفيف إجراءات دخول مواطني أوغندا بعد انتهاء تفشي إيبولا - بوابة الشروق
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The UAE announces easing of entry procedures for Ugandan nationals after the Ebola outbreak ends - Al Shorouk Portal
article.articleSummary: Uganda Ebola outbreak ends; UAE eases entry procedures for Ugandan nationals. The National Emergency Crisis and Disasters Management Authority announced that entry precautions applied in June in response to Ebola developments will be relaxed, based on ongoing epidemiological assessment and latest public-health updates, including Uganda’s declaration that the Ebola outbreak has ended after completing the internationally approved monitoring period. Precautions for travellers from the Democratic Republic of Congo and South Sudan remain in force due to ongoing Ebola activity there. UAE authorities, including the Ministry of Health and Prevention, the Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship, and border-security bodies, will continue to monitor regional and international Ebola developments. Measures will be reviewed regularly and adjusted as risk assessments and public-health standards evolve to ensure proportional protection.

triage.headline_ja: UAE、ウガンダのエボラ流行終息を受けてウガンダ国民の入国手続きを緩和
triage.triage_reason: 記事の主題はウガンダのエボラ終息とUAEの渡航制限緩和だが、DRCおよび南スーダンで引き続きエボラ活動が継続していると言及されており、詳細不明のため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はウガンダのエボラ終息宣言とそれに伴うUAEの入国制限緩和。DRCと南スーダンでは引き続きエボラ活動があるとされているが、南スーダンは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCでの継続状況の詳細（症例数・重症度等）は本記事からは不明。

article.articleHeadline: 26/9 in Nieuwsuur: Ebola in Congo * De toekomst van de VN
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 26/9 on Nieuwsuur: Ebola in the Congo • The Future of the UN
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo variant of Ebola continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with at least 3,799 deaths, primarily among young children, making it the deadliest Ebola outbreak on record. Correspondent Elles van Gelder visited an Ebola clinic in northeastern DRC to report on the crisis. Concurrently, the United Nations General Assembly in New York gathered leaders including Donald Trump and Rob Jetten, prompting questions about the value and future of the UN in 2026. Critics argue the UN is cumbersome, outdated, and expensive, with developing economies underrepresented and critical issues decided by five powers. The piece presents the debate with input from historian and geopolitics analyst Alex Krijger.

article.articleHeadline: Focarul de Ebola se extinde în RD Congo. Aproape 3.800 de oameni au murit, iar 63 de zone sunt afectate - Știrile ProTV
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak is spreading in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Almost 3,800 people have died, and 63 areas are affected - ProTV News.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues, with 7,890 confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths reported by WHO as of September 23, affecting 63 areas. Zones affected include Bulu in Sud-Ubangi and Dungu in Haut-Uele, border areas near South Sudan. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that regional conflict and population displacement impede medical access, contact tracing, safe burials, and reaching those at risk. Although case numbers are falling and contact tracing and safe burials have improved, transmission remains uneven across affected areas. The lack of vaccines and approved treatments for the Bundibugyo strain complicates response and may drive reluctance to seek care. WHO is accelerating clinical studies for vaccines and therapies. The article also references ongoing pandemic preparedness discussions, including the May 2025 Pandemic Accord, and notes WHO refutes claims that it cedes sovereignty.

article.articleHeadline: Sarampión se dispara en Perú: casos se duplicaron en mes y medio y advierten que podrían cuadruplicarse
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Measles spike in Peru: cases doubled in a month and a half, and authorities warn they could quadruple.
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreak in Peru could worsen, with cases doubling from 1,236 on July 26 to about 2,400, according to health authorities. The Ministry of Health logged 1,747 confirmed cases in epidemiological week 33, while unofficial updates note rising totals. Puno leads with 1,264 cases, followed by Arequipa (292); Cusco and Madre de Dios also report cases. A 16-year-old unvaccinated resident of Alto Monte, San Pablo, Ramón Castilla, Loreto, died from measles complications including pneumonia—the country’s first measles death in 23 years. Experts warn cases could triple or quadruple in the next month, especially in the Amazon region with low vaccination coverage. Vaccination gaps are widening: first-dose coverage down ~80%, second-dose ~75%. About 50–60% of cases are 10–29 years old; in San Pablo, around 40% are 16–26. Coordinated government action, potentially an emergency declaration, is urged, as Loreto’s remote communities face access barriers.

Separately, doctors note a recent COVID-19 outbreak in Thailand but say there is no risk of an epidemic there or globally at this time. Details such as patient numbers, transmission mode, and laboratory findings are not provided. The absence of a confirmed etiological link raises public health concerns while authorities await testing results.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The UAE allocates $10 million to combat Ebola in Africa
article.articleSummary: The United Arab Emirates earmarked $10 million through the UAE International Aid Agency to curb the Ebola outbreak in Africa, announced by President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan during an international meeting called by the United States at the UN General Assembly. The initiative aims to strengthen health-response capacities in affected areas as Ebola continues to challenge the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with expanding geographic spread. UAE has dispatched over 150 tons of aid, including protective equipment, infection-control supplies, shelter materials, and food, benefiting about 280 health facilities and vulnerable groups such as women and children. Dr. Tariq Ahmed Al Ameri, head of the UAE International Aid Agency, stressed international coordination and rapid action to prevent transmission and bolster early detection and outbreak response capabilities.

article.articleHeadline: जलभराव व जलजनित संक्रमणों से किडनी की सेहत पर बढ़ा खतरा
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Flooding and waterborne infections increase the risk to renal health.
article.articleSummary: Flooding in Lucknow has raised concerns about water quality and waterborne infections, with increased risk to renal health, according to Dr. Anand Tripathi, Chief Medical Superintendent at Thakurganj Combined TB Hospital. Contaminated water and food can spread diarrhea, gastroenteritis, typhoid, and hepatitis A and E. Severe diarrhea and vomiting cause dehydration and electrolyte loss, potentially reducing renal blood flow and heightening the risk of acute kidney injury, while systemic infections can also impair kidney function. For patients with pre-existing kidney disease, clinicians may assess renal function during severe waterborne illnesses. Monsoon advisories stress safeguarding drinking water: boil or filter water before use and avoid water from unregulated tanks, open vessels, or other suspect sources to mitigate renal risk.

article.articleSummary: Two suspected gastroenteritis cases, involving eight people, were reported by Macau health authorities on 26 September 2026 linked to The Parisian Macao buffet on Cotai. The eight diners consumed dishes such as cheese-baked lobster, steamed scallops, and abalone tart, and later experienced fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Based on dining records, incubation period, and symptoms, a bacterial pathogen is considered the more likely cause. Authorities have visited the venue, collected food and environmental samples for laboratory testing, and issued preventive control measures, including stopping sale of implicated foods and carrying out cleaning and disinfection of the premises. The investigation aims to identify the source and prevent further cases; no fatalities are reported in the article.

article.articleHeadline: Coimbatore corporation holds dengue street awareness programmes
article.articleSummary: Coimbatore corporation conducted dengue street awareness programmes in five zones of Coimbatore on 26 September 2026, engaging over 500 residents including students. The events took place along South Second Street (Avarampalayam), AKS Nagar near Gandhi Park, Itteri Road (Pothanur), Kallarai Road (Sowripalayam), and Ramalingam Colony near Bharathi Park. Activities transformed streets into dengue-awareness zones with messages on prevention, mosquito control, and public health. Highlights included dengue-awareness short films, a public pledge 'Let us participate and eradicate dengue,' demonstrations of mosquito-control equipment, and displays of containers that can breed mosquitoes. Also featured were dengue-story street plays, rangoli competitions, door-to-door pamphlets by seniors, fever-screening camps by mobile medical teams, distribution of nilavembu herbal drink, and saplings planting. Officials said similar programmes would be held weekly across 6,959 streets; residents cautioned about waste management during peak seasons to prevent outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: 7 Gejala Influenza Tipe A yang Perlu Dikenali dan Cara Mengatasinya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 7 Symptoms of Influenza Type A You Should Recognize and How to Manage Them
article.articleSummary: As of 26 September 2026, Influenza Type A causes abrupt respiratory illness, typically heavier than seasonal flu, with most cases improving at home within about a week. Symptoms are described as sudden and may include fever and body aches; duration generally 3–7 days. Risk factors include close contact with infected individuals, immunocompromise, chronic diseases (asthma, diabetes, heart disease), and age groups under 5 or over 65. Management emphasizes rest and fluids; paracetamol or ibuprofen can relieve fever and pain. Antivirals such as oseltamivir or zanamivir may be prescribed for more severe cases. Transmission occurs via droplets and contaminated hands. Prevention: stay home when ill, wear masks in crowds, ensure ventilation, avoid crowded closed spaces, and practice hand hygiene. Seek medical care if symptoms worsen or in pregnancy, elderly, young children, or chronic disease, per guidance from WHO, CDC, Primaya Hospital, and Indonesia's Ministry of Health.

article.articleHeadline: Global analysis maps Staphylococcus aureus burden and antibiotic resistance
article.articleSummary: Staphylococcus aureus accounts for about a quarter of bovine intramammary infections (mastitis) globally, drawn from 143 studies (2010–2025) across 40 countries. Global prevalence estimated at 24.78% (95% CI 21.27–28.47), with Africa 29.21%, North America 28.15%, Asia 25.88%, Europe 14.19%, and Oceania 5.27%. Country-level highs include Cameroon 67%, Sri Lanka 64.32%, Indonesia 56.98%, Mexico 48%, Japan 47.44%, Uruguay 47.07%; lows include Poland 0.70%, Australia 5.49%, New Zealand 5.32%. Prevalence rose through 2014–2018, peaking in 2018 (41.39%), with recent years often higher, possibly due to improved surveillance and larger dairy herds. Antimicrobial resistance is alarmingly high: penicillin 65.19%, ampicillin 62.80%, amoxicillin 52.07%; doxycycline 70.73%, oxytetracycline 62.42%; oxacillin 40.23% and vancomycin 44.62% show notable resistance. Resistance genes blaZ, mecA, ermC/B, msrA, mphC, tetK/L/M are common, frequently carried on mobile elements, signaling multidrug resistance and challenging mastitis control.

article.articleSummary: Ukraine reports a spread of an unknown infection not resembling influenza or COVID-19. Early signs include severe allergy-like symptoms, cough, and low-grade fever; within days, a weakened patient may develop a bacterial superinfection. There has been no confirmation from Ukraine’s Ministry of Health, though physician Taras Zhiravetsky acknowledged rapid spread. Official statements cited by the state TV channel Star claim that only already known diseases — including influenza and COVID-19 — are circulating. In Russia, Rospotrebnadzor tightened controls to prevent introduction of endemic typhus following an outbreak in Los Angeles. Separately, Chinese researchers identified a new virus transmitted to humans by bites of the Asian long-horned tick Haemaphysalis longicornis, named ALTNV (Asian longhorned tick nairovirus). The study notes uncertainty about ALTNV’s spread to Russia; coverage by Evening Moscow explored potential implications.

article.articleHeadline: 65 Kasus Flu Babi H1N1 Terdeteksi di Bandung
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 65 H1N1 Swine Flu Cases Detected in Bandung
article.articleSummary: 65 laboratory-confirmed Influenza A (H1N1) swine flu cases detected in Bandung, West Java, as of 26 September 2026, via Whole Genome Sequencing by Labkes Jabar; true community incidence likely higher due to limited testing access. Influenza A (H1N1) is described as highly transmissible with more severe symptoms than seasonal flu, including high fever, headache, dizziness, and marked fatigue, contributing to rising hospital occupancy in Bandung due to patient demand. No deaths reported in West Java to date, but vulnerable groups—children and individuals with comorbidities such as heart disease, diabetes, tuberculosis, and HIV—remain at risk. Public guidance urges seeking care if symptoms persist beyond three days, and calls for strict Clean and Healthy Living Behaviors (PHBS): masking in crowds, frequent handwashing, home isolation, and utilization of influenza vaccination to curb transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Lucknow on dengue, malaria alert after three days of rain
article.articleSummary: Lucknow faces elevated risk of dengue, malaria, and chikungunya after three days of rain and waterlogging. Surveillance and preventive measures have been intensified across eight zones; malaria inspectors and teams conduct house-to-house surveillance, identify breeding sites, and carry out source reduction, with around 250 households checked on September 25. Notices are issued to premises with larvae. Multiple medical mobile units remain deployed for consultation and medicines. The Chief Medical Officer has ordered urban and rural health centres to maintain adequate stocks of medicines, including anti-snake venom, and for hospitals to stay on alert for vector-borne illnesses. District malaria officer Ritu Srivastava notes rain may wash out some larvae and lower humidity, but the crucial period is after the rains stop when anti-larval spraying and fogging resume. Lucknow has 110 wards and five malaria inspectors; January 2026–present data show 255 dengue, 251 malaria, 18 chikungunya; no Japanese Encephalitis in four years.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cleanup drive will be held in Aracitaba to combat the dengue mosquito's breeding grounds.
article.articleSummary: Aracitaba will stage a citywide cleanup on Thursday, October 1, to remove items that can accumulate water and serve as breeding grounds for Aedes aegypti, the dengue vector. A municipal collection truck will traverse the town to gather debris, tires, bottles and other objects that can hold standing water. Residents are urged to prepare by cleaning their yards in advance and placing discarded materials at the curb in front of their homes to facilitate pickup. The initiative is part of ongoing dengue prevention and control efforts in the municipality, aiming to reduce mosquito habitats and lower transmission risk. Community participation is essential for reaching multiple neighborhoods. Report from Jornal Panorama, based on information from the Aracitaba City Hall.

article.articleHeadline: Five months after elephant calf's anthrax death in MP, Bandhavgarh steps up surveillance
article.articleSummary: Gayatri, a four-year-old female elephant calf at Tala Camp, Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve, Madhya Pradesh, died April 28 with symptoms suggestive of anthrax; lab confirmation by SWFH, Jabalpur, made it MP’s first confirmed wild-elephant anthrax death. Five months later, during Bandhavgarh’s five-day Hathi Mahotsava, 15 captive-trained elephants remain under round-the-clock monitoring. Precautions included cremation of Gayatri without autopsy, relocation of Tala camp elephants, quarantine and fencing of the death site, destruction of contaminated material, and vaccination of all 15 elephants after vaccines were obtained from Bengaluru with help from a Bhopal lab; staff received prophylactic antibiotics. Umaria district launched a bovine vaccination drive in villages adjoining the Tala core zone to reduce cross-species transmission. Anthrax spores persist in soil for decades, underpinning the long-term risk and need for SOPs and surveillance. The episode joins a history of wildlife anthrax outbreaks in India, such as Similipal (2016) and Dehing Patkai (2020).
